slides.title: Partner approval [isn't evidence.]
slides.lede: A proposed position can win unanimous partner approval and still be indistinguishable from the competition. Test it with buyers before you commit.

slides.title: Do buyers know what you stand for and [who you serve]?

cards.label: Preference
cards.text: "It sounds professional." Positive, but it hasn't changed their understanding.

cards.label: Comprehension
cards.text: Buyers accurately describe your intended specialism and who you serve.

slides.title: Is it a problem buyers [actually want solved]?
slides.note: "I like this" is not a request for a proposal. **Actions are stronger signals**, though none proves willingness to pay.

slides.title: Put a competitor's name on your statement. [Still convincing?]
slides.text: If it is, the language is generic and needs greater specificity. Compare the evidence behind each claim, not simply the wording.

slides.title: Can you [prove] every claim you make?

items.title: Industry specialist
items.text: Relevant sector experience and documented client work

slides.title: Approve, refine or reject [before you design] anything

items.title: Approve
items.text: Proceed to brand strategy and identity development.

items.title: Refine
items.text: Adjust the positioning and repeat the relevant research.

items.title: Reject
items.text: Return to the strategic work. Not a failed rebrand.

slides.title: A brand position should change the buying conversation.
slides.lede: Brand positioning testing before investing in a rebrand. Read the full guide via the link in our bio.
